briefs: Gérard Depardieu will face trial for rape, a French court rules. (Reuters)
Sweden's Centre leader backs a right-wing prime minister in a major shift. (Reuters)
Türkiye's elections set for 2028 as the ruling alliance agrees on an Erdoğan candidacy. (Reuters)
Poland's defence ministry to sign an AI decision-support deal with Palantir on Friday. (Reuters)
Ebola cases in DR Congo pass 10,000 in the fastest-growing outbreak on record. (Wire reports)
Iraqi Kurds protest Baghdad's moves to assert central control over their region. (Reuters)
Early voting opens in New Zealand's 2026 election, with polls pointing to a tight race. (Wire reports)
Algeria approves a troop deployment to Niger — its first foreign mission since 1973. (Wire reports)
compiled: Compiled from wire reports filed 26–27 Nov 2026 — Reuters, Associated Press, BBC News and Al Jazeera — as of 02:00 UTC, Thursday 27 November 2026.
datelines: Russian missiles and drones struck residential districts overnight; Zelenskyy warns a major attack on the power grid is imminent.
Intercepted Iranian drones rained debris on an air-defence station, killing two Italian technicians; Iran denies involvement.
Five strikes and a shooting killed 10 Palestinians, among them a Hamas official and his wife, hospital officials said.
A fuel tanker crash ignited a massive fire on a highway ringing the capital, killing at least 31 people. (AP)
Police used tear gas against garment workers protesting for the second day over pay and conditions.
edition: The World Today — One Image Edition

lead.deck: Washington unveiled a broad new tariff package aimed at China, the European Union, Brazil, Taiwan and 11 other economies, accusing them of flooding world markets with subsidized industrial production. Beijing threatened retaliation within hours, and rattled exporters from Brasília to Brussels began weighing their response.
lead.headline: US Proposes New Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners Over Subsidized Factories

numbers: 14 — trading partners in the new US tariff plan
€1.58tn — EU budget left undecided in Brussels
€45bn — Ukraine loan deadlocked at the summit
31 — killed in the Cairo tanker fire
10 — killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
500,000 — Russian troops reported killed in Ukraine

second.deck: Debris from intercepted drones fell on an air-defence station in Kuwait, killing two Italian radar technicians and wounding two others. Kuwait and Rome blamed Iran; Tehran called the charge a pretext for war. Hours earlier, an attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery killed a Nepali worker and halted some operations, leaving the Gulf on edge.
second.headline: Drone Strike Kills Two Italian Technicians in Kuwait; Iran Denies Any Role

items: Attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery kills a Nepali worker, starts a fire and halts some operations at the 400,000-barrel-a-day plant. (Reuters)
Israeli strikes kill 10 people across Gaza, hospital officials say, as Hamas weighs its response. (Reuters)
Saudi airstrikes hit Sanaa overnight as the Houthis and the kingdom trade near-daily blows in Yemen's revived war. (AP)
sections.name: MIDDLE EAST & THE GULF

items: EU leaders end a 12-hour Brussels summit deadlocked over the €1.58 trillion 2028–34 budget and a €45 billion loan for Ukraine; talks resume December 17–18. (AP)
Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos is chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank. (Reuters)
Bank of England to cut capital requirements for UK-focused lenders in a post-crisis rule rethink. (Reuters)
sections.name: EUROPE

items: Russian ballistic missiles and more than 100 drones strike Kyiv and Kharkiv overnight, killing at least three people. (Wire reports)
Leaked Russian records suggest nearly 500,000 Russian soldiers have died in Ukraine since the 2022 invasion. (Analysis)
Russia arrests a deputy aerospace commander in a reported corruption case. (Reuters)
sections.name: UKRAINE & RUSSIA

items: Severe weather on both coasts complicates Thanksgiving travel for millions of Americans. (AP)
Trump uses his Thanksgiving message to lash out at political foes, immigrants and the federal government. (Reuters)
Trump calls revised GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of the Commerce Department. (AP)
sections.name: UNITED STATES

items: North Korea's Kim Jong Un vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's latest overture. (AP)
Police fire tear gas to disperse fresh protests by Bangladesh garment workers. (Reuters)
North Korean launderers turn to little-known crypto services to move the Binance haul, researchers say. (Reuters)
sections.name: ASIA-PACIFIC

items: Altria, the US maker of Marlboro, explores an all-cash bid for Imperial Brands in a possible tobacco carve-up. (Reuters)
Dutch groups ask a court to halt sales of Meta's smart glasses in the Netherlands over privacy concerns. (Reuters)
FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centres in space; scientists are sceptical. (AP)
